claims.claim: Expression of KibS677A-GFP under the nub>Gal4 driver leads to significantly smaller adult wings than wild-type Kib-GFP.
claims.source: Consistent with the observed increased protein abundance, expression of KibS677A-GFP under the nub>Gal4 driver led to significantly smaller adult wings than did wild-type Kib-GFP (Figure 3I and J).
claims.evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3I and J.

claims.claim: Slimb regulates Kib stability in vivo.
claims.source: Collectively, these results indicate that Slimb regulates Kib stability in vivo.
claims.evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from multiple lines of experimental evidence.

claims.claim: Ubiquitination of KibS677A is not sensitive to depletion of Hpo and Wts.
claims.source: In striking contrast to wild-type Kib, ubiquitination of KibS677A was not sensitive to depletion of Hpo and Wts (Figure 3E), suggesting that the Hpo pathway promotes Kib degradation via Slimb-mediated ubiquitination.
claims.evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3E.

claims.claim: The Hpo pathway promotes Kib degradation via Slimb-mediated ubiquitination.
claims.source: In striking contrast to wild-type Kib, ubiquitination of KibS677A was not sensitive to depletion of Hpo and Wts (Figure 3E), suggesting that the Hpo pathway promotes Kib degradation via Slimb-mediated ubiquitination.
claims.evidence: This is an inference drawn from the observation that the degron mutant is insensitive to pathway inactivation.

claims.claim: UASp-Kib-GFP is dramatically upregulated apically and basally in Mer clones relative to control cells.
claims.source: Similar to endogenous Kib (Figure 1B) or Kib expressed by the ubiquitin promoter (Figure 2B), UASp-Kib-GFP was dramatically upregulated apically and basally in Mer clones relative to control cells (Figure 4A–C' and G).
claims.evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4A-C' and G.

claims.claim: KibS677A-GFP appears only mildly apically stabilized in Mer clones.
claims.source: In contrast, KibS677A-GFP appeared only mildly apically stabilized in Mer clones (Figure 4D–E'), with no detectible difference in basal KibS677A-GFP levels between the clone and control cells (Figure 4F–F' and H).
claims.evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4D-F' and H.

claims.claim: There is no detectable difference in basal KibS677A-GFP levels between Mer clones and control cells.
claims.source: In contrast, KibS677A-GFP appeared only mildly apically stabilized in Mer clones (Figure 4D–E'), with no detectible difference in basal KibS677A-GFP levels between the clone and control cells (Figure 4F–F' and H).
claims.evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4F-F' and H.

claims.claim: The Hpo pathway regulates Kib levels via the degron motif.
claims.source: Taken together, these results indicate that the Hpo pathway regulates Kib levels via the degron motif.
claims.evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the differential behavior of wild-type Kib and KibS677A in Mer clones.

claims.claim: Wild-type Kib-GFP increases both apically and basally in hpo clones.
claims.source: Strikingly, whereas wild-type Kib-GFP increased both apically and basally in hpo clones (Figure 4I–K' and O), KibS677A-GFP increased apically but decreased basally in hpo clones (Figure 4L–N' and P).
claims.evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4I-K' and O.

claims.claim: KibS677A-GFP increases apically but decreases basally in hpo clones.
claims.source: Strikingly, whereas wild-type Kib-GFP increased both apically and basally in hpo clones (Figure 4I–K' and O), KibS677A-GFP increased apically but decreased basally in hpo clones (Figure 4L–N' and P).
claims.evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4L-N' and P.

claims.claim: The stabilization of KibS677A-GFP upon Hpo pathway inactivation is, at least in part, due to the recruitment of Kib apically.
claims.source: These results suggest that the stabilization of KibS677A-GFP observed upon Hpo pathway inactivation is, at least in part, due to the recruitment of Kib apically, where it might be stabilized in a protein complex.
claims.evidence: This is an inference drawn from the observation that KibS677A increases apically but decreases basally in hpo clones.

claims.claim: Depletion of Ex and Crb, either individually or together, has no detectable effect on Ubi>Kib-GFP levels.
claims.source: To our surprise, depletion of Ex and Crb, either individually or together, had no detectable effect on Ubi>Kib-GFP levels (Figure 5A–C').
claims.evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5A-C'.

claims.claim: Reducing Hpo pathway activity by overexpressing Dachs or depleting Fat, Ds, or Tao-1 has no effect on Ubi>Kib-GFP levels.
claims.source: Moreover, reducing Hpo pathway activity by other means, such as by overexpressing Dachs or depleting Fat, Ds, or the Hpo activator Tao-1 (Boggiano et al., 2011), similarly had no effect on Ubi>Kib-GFP levels (Figure 5—figure supplement 1A–E).
claims.evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1A-E.

claims.claim: Knockdown of Mats or Pez increases Ubi>Kib-GFP levels.
claims.source: On the other hand, knockdown of Mats' or Kib's binding partner, Pez (Poernbacher et al., 2012), increased Ubi>Kib-GFP levels (Figure 5—figure supplement 1F–G).
claims.evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1F-G.

claims.claim: Upstream regulation of the Hpo pathway is highly compartmentalized.
claims.source: These results suggest that upstream regulation of the Hpo pathway is highly compartmentalized and that Kib degradation is promoted specifically via the pathway components it associates with during Hpo pathway activation.
claims.evidence: This is an inference drawn from the observation that only certain pathway components affect Kib levels.

claims.claim: Kib degradation is promoted specifically via the pathway components it associates with during Hpo pathway activation.
claims.source: These results suggest that upstream regulation of the Hpo pathway is highly compartmentalized and that Kib degradation is promoted specifically via the pathway components it associates with during Hpo pathway activation.
claims.evidence: This is an inference drawn from the selective effects of different pathway components on Kib levels.

claims.claim: Ubi>Kib-GFP strongly suppresses exe1 lethality.
claims.source: Ubi>Kib-GFP strongly suppressed exe1 lethality, producing viable and fertile adult flies at expected frequencies (Figure 5—figure supplement 1I) that completely lacked Ex protein (Figure 5—figure supplement 1J–K').
claims.evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1I-K'.

claims.claim: Homozygous exe1; Ubi>-Kib-GFP/+ flies have significantly larger wings than heterozygotes.
claims.source: Homozygous exe1; Ubi>-Kib-GFP/+ flies had significantly larger wings than heterozygotes (Figure 5D–E), but otherwise were phenotypically normal.
claims.evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5D-E.

claims.claim: Kib and Ex signal in parallel to regulate at least some aspects of pathway activity.
claims.source: Together, these results establish that Kib and Ex signal in parallel to regulate at least some aspects of pathway activity.
claims.evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the rescue of ex mutants by Kib overexpression.

claims.claim: Expression of HpoK71R or WtsK743R restores Kib ubiquitination when the endogenous kinases are depleted.
claims.source: To our surprise, expression of HpoK71R or WtsK743R restored Kib ubiquitination when the endogenous kinases were depleted, indicating that these kinases promote Kib ubiquitination via complex formation rather than phosphorylation (Figure 2I).
claims.evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2I.

claims.claim: Hpo and Wts promote Kib ubiquitination via complex formation rather than phosphorylation.
claims.source: To our surprise, expression of HpoK71R or WtsK743R restored Kib ubiquitination when the endogenous kinases were depleted, indicating that these kinases promote Kib ubiquitination via complex formation rather than phosphorylation (Figure 2I).
claims.evidence: This is an inference drawn from the observation that kinase-dead versions can restore ubiquitination.

claims.claim: Kib is a multivalent adaptor protein that contains two N-terminal WW domains (WW1 and WW2), a C2-like domain, a putative atypical protein kinase C (aPKC)-binding domain, and three coiled-coil regions (CC1, CC2, and CC3).
claims.source: Kib is a multivalent adaptor protein that contains at least seven potential functional regions: two N-terminal WW domains (WW1 and WW2), a C2-like domain, a putative atypical protein kinase C (aPKC)-binding domain, and three coiled-coil regions (CC1, CC2, and CC3; Figure 6A).
claims.evidence: This describes the known domain structure of Kibra.

claims.claim: A Kib truncation lacking the C-terminal third of the coding sequence (Kib1-857-GFP) is strongly upregulated upon Hpo depletion.
claims.source: A Kib truncation lacking the C-terminal third of the coding sequence (Kib1-857-GFP) but retaining the degron motif was strongly upregulated upon Hpo depletion, similar to wild-type Kib (Figure 6—figure supplement 1A–B').
claims.evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1A-B'.

claims.claim: Flies expressing Kib1-857-GFP have smaller wings than those expressing wild-type Kib-GFP.
claims.source: Flies expressing Kib1-857-GFP had smaller wings than those expressing wild-type Kib-GFP (Figure 6—figure supplement 1K), suggesting that deletion of the C-terminal region enhances Kib activity.
claims.evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1K.

claims.claim: A Kib truncation lacking the first 483 aa (Kib484-1288-GFP) is insensitive to Hpo depletion.
claims.source: In contrast, a Kib truncation lacking the first 483 aa (Kib484-1288-GFP) was insensitive to Hpo depletion even though it retained the Slimb degron motif (Figure 6—figure supplement 1D and D'), suggesting that the degron alone is not sufficient for pathway-mediated degradation of Kib.
claims.evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1D and D'.

claims.claim: The degron alone is not sufficient for pathway-mediated degradation of Kib.
claims.source: In contrast, a Kib truncation lacking the first 483 aa (Kib484-1288-GFP) was insensitive to Hpo depletion even though it retained the Slimb degron motif (Figure 6—figure supplement 1D and D'), suggesting that the degron alone is not sufficient for pathway-mediated degradation of Kib.
claims.evidence: This is an inference drawn from the observation that Kib484-1288 retains the degron but is not degraded.

claims.claim: The first 483 amino acids of Kib are essential for Hpo pathway activation.
claims.source: Interestingly, Kib484-1288-GFP was much less potent at suppressing wing growth compared to wild-type Kib-GFP (Figure 6—figure supplement 1K), indicating that the first 483 amino acids of Kib are also essential for Hpo pathway activation.
claims.evidence: This is an inference drawn from the observation that Kib484-1288 has reduced growth suppression activity.

claims.claim: Deletion of either CC1 or CC2 does not prevent Kib upregulation upon Hpo depletion.
claims.source: Deletion of either CC1 or CC2 did not prevent Kib upregulation upon Hpo depletion, indicating that these regions do not mediate pathway-dependent Kib degradation (Figure 6—figure supplement 1E–F').
claims.evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1E-F'.

claims.claim: Kib variants lacking the WW domains express at markedly higher levels than wild-type Kib.
claims.source: However, Kib variants lacking the WW domains, either individually (KibΔWW1-GFP and KibΔWW2-GFP) or together (KibΔWW1&2-GFP), expressed at markedly higher levels than wild-type Kib (Figure 6B).
claims.evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6B.

claims.claim: Kib variants lacking the WW domains are not upregulated when Hpo is depleted.
claims.source: Additionally, these proteins accumulated at the junctional cortex and appeared to be depleted basally but were not upregulated when Hpo was depleted (Figure 6C–C'' and Figure 6—figure supplement 1G–I').
claims.evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6C-C'' and Figure 6—figure supplement 1G-I'.

claims.claim: The WW domains of Kib are necessary for its degradation via the Hpo pathway.
claims.source: Thus, the WW domains of Kib are necessary for its degradation via the Hpo pathway.
claims.evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the observation that WW domain deletions prevent pathway-mediated degradation.

claims.claim: Kib lacking the WW domains interacts with Slimb normally in S2 cells.
claims.source: Importantly, while Kib lacking the WW domains interacted with Slimb normally in S2 cells (Figure 6—figure supplement 2A), depletion of Slimb had no effect on KibΔWW1-GFP levels (Figure 6D–D''), again suggesting that association between Kib and Slimb alone is not sufficient for Kib degradation.
claims.evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 2A.

claims.claim: Depletion of Slimb has no effect on KibΔWW1-GFP levels.
claims.source: Importantly, while Kib lacking the WW domains interacted with Slimb normally in S2 cells (Figure 6—figure supplement 2A), depletion of Slimb had no effect on KibΔWW1-GFP levels (Figure 6D–D''), again suggesting that association between Kib and Slimb alone is not sufficient for Kib degradation.
claims.evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6D-D''.

claims.claim: Association between Kib and Slimb alone is not sufficient for Kib degradation.
claims.source: Importantly, while Kib lacking the WW domains interacted with Slimb normally in S2 cells (Figure 6—figure supplement 2A), depletion of Slimb had no effect on KibΔWW1-GFP levels (Figure 6D–D''), again suggesting that association between Kib and Slimb alone is not sufficient for Kib degradation.
claims.evidence: This is an inference drawn from the observation that WW domain deletions prevent degradation despite maintaining Slimb interaction.

claims.claim: Slimb co-immunoprecipitates with Mer, Hpo, and Wts in S2 cells.
claims.source: Consistent with this prediction, Slimb co-immunoprecipitated with Mer, Hpo, and Wts in S2 cells (Figure 6—figure supplement 2B–D).
claims.evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 2B-D.

claims.claim: Deletion of both WW domains enhances Kib interaction with Mer in S2 cells.
claims.source: A previous study found that deletion of both WW domains enhanced Kib interaction with Mer in S2 cells (Baumgartner et al., 2010), a result we confirmed (Figure 6—figure supplement 2E).
claims.evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 2E and a citation to prior research.

claims.claim: The interaction of KibΔWW1&2 with Wts is significantly weakened.
claims.source: We found that the interaction of KibΔWW1&2 with Wts was significantly weakened (Figure 6—figure supplement 2F).
claims.evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 2F.

claims.claim: Pez interacts with Kib via the WW domains in S2 cells.
claims.source: Additionally, it was previously reported that Pez interacts with Kib via the WW domains in S2 cells (Poernbacher et al., 2012), consistent with our in vivo observation that loss of Pez leads to higher Kib levels.
claims.evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior research.

claims.claim: Ectopically expressed wild-type Kib-GFP appears more abundant at the center of the wing pouch with a marked decrease in fluorescence at the tissue periphery.
claims.source: Ectopically expressed wild-type Kib-GFP appeared more abundant at the center of the wing pouch with a marked decrease in fluorescence at the tissue periphery (Figure 7A and A').
claims.evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figure 7A and A'.

claims.claim: Ectopically expressed KibS677A-GFP fluorescence is distributed more uniformly throughout the wing pouch.
claims.source: In contrast, ectopically expressed KibS677A-GFP fluorescence was distributed more uniformly throughout the wing pouch (Figure 7B and B' and Figure 7—figure supplement 1B–D).
claims.evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figure 7B and B' and Figure 7—figure supplement 1B-D.

claims.claim: The difference between Kib and KibS677A abundance throughout the tissue is likely a result of differential protein turnover.
claims.source: Because both transgenes were expressed from identical genomic locations and under the same ectopic promoter, we reasoned that the difference between Kib and KibS677A abundance throughout the tissue was likely a result of differential protein turnover.
claims.evidence: This is an inference drawn from the experimental design and observations.

claims.claim: Expression of KibS677A inhibits wing growth disproportionately more in the proximal region.
claims.source: Strikingly, while the relative decrease in width distally was mild in nub>UASp-Kib-GFP or nub>UASp-KibS677A-GFP wings compared to control wings, the proximal width decreased dramatically in wings expressing KibS677A, indicating that expression of KibS677A inhibited growth disproportionately more in the proximal region (Figure 7C).
claims.evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figure 7C.

claims.claim: Kib degradation occurs in a patterned manner in the wing imaginal epithelium.
claims.source: Collectively, these results suggest that Kib degradation occurs in a patterned manner in the wing imaginal epithelium and could serve to pattern growth of this tissue.
claims.evidence: This is an inference drawn from the differential distribution of Kib and KibS677A and their effects on wing growth.

claims.claim: The pattern of Kib degradation is similar to the pattern of junctional tension in the wing blade.
claims.source: The pattern of Kib degradation we observe, higher at the periphery and lower in the center, is similar to the pattern of junctional tension in the wing blade reported previously (Legoff et al., 2013; Mao et al., 2013).
claims.evidence: This is a comparison to prior research supported by citations.

claims.claim: Higher levels of Kib-GFP are observed within bantam clones.
claims.source: Indeed, we observed higher levels of Kib-GFP within bantam clones (Figure 7E–G''').
claims.evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figure 7E-G'''.

claims.claim: KibΔWW1-GFP levels do not change in bantam clones.
claims.source: Importantly, KibΔWW1-GFP levels did not change in bantam clones (Figure 7H–I'), as expected if tension-induced Kib degradation requires Kib-mediated Hpo signaling complex formation.
claims.evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figure 7H-I'.

claims.claim: Kib degradation is patterned by mechanical tension across the wing pouch.
claims.source: Taken together, these results suggest that Kib degradation is patterned by mechanical tension across the wing pouch resulting in decreased Kib in regions of high tension and greater Yki promoted growth.
claims.evidence: This is an inference drawn from the bantam clone experiments and comparison to tension patterns.

claims.claim: The Hpo pathway negatively regulates Kib levels via a post-translational feedback loop.
claims.source: In this study, we show that the Hpo pathway negatively regulates Kib levels via a previously unrecognized post-translational feedback loop.
claims.evidence: This is a summary of the main finding of the study.

claims.claim: Loss of Mer leads to a dramatic increase in Kib levels without a detectable increase in Yki transcriptional activity.
claims.source: First, loss of Mer leads to a dramatic increase in Kib levels without a detectable increase in Yki transcriptional activity.
claims.evidence: This is a summary of experimental findings from the study.

claims.claim: Removing Sd does not suppress the elevated Kib levels upon Hpo pathway inactivation.
claims.source: Second, removing Sd, which blocks Yki-mediated transcription, does not suppress the elevated Kib levels upon Hpo pathway inactivation.
claims.evidence: This is a summary of experimental findings from the study.

claims.claim: The abundance of Kib-GFP expressed under a Yki-insensitive promoter increases upon Hpo pathway inactivation.
claims.source: Third, the abundance of Kib-GFP expressed under a Yki-insensitive promoter (Ubi>Kib-GFP) still increases upon Hpo pathway inactivation.
claims.evidence: This is a summary of experimental findings from the study.

claims.claim: Kib ubiquitination is mediated via SCFSlimb.
claims.source: Additionally, we show that Kib is phosphorylated and ubiquitinated in a pathway-dependent manner, and that Kib ubiquitination is mediated via SCFSlimb.
claims.evidence: This is a summary of experimental findings from the study.

claims.claim: Kib degradation by the Hpo pathway is insulated from the activity of other upstream pathway regulators.
claims.source: A striking aspect of our findings is the extent to which Kib degradation by the Hpo pathway is insulated from the activity of other upstream pathway regulators.
claims.evidence: This is a summary of experimental findings from the study.

claims.claim: Crb and Ex function together at the junctional cortex.
claims.source: Previous studies have shown that Crb and Ex function together at the junctional cortex (Chen et al., 2010; Ling et al., 2010; Robinson et al., 2010; Sun et al., 2015) and in parallel to Kib at the medial cortex (Su et al., 2017).
claims.evidence: This is supported by citations to prior research.

claims.claim: Ft can influence Ex stability at the junctions.
claims.source: Ft can influence Ex stability at the junctions (Silva et al., 2006; Wang et al., 2019), suggesting linkage between these Hpo signaling branches, and Tao-1 functions downstream of Ex (Chung et al., 2016).
claims.evidence: This is supported by citations to prior research.

claims.claim: Tao-1 functions downstream of Ex.
claims.source: Ft can influence Ex stability at the junctions (Silva et al., 2006; Wang et al., 2019), suggesting linkage between these Hpo signaling branches, and Tao-1 functions downstream of Ex (Chung et al., 2016).
claims.evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior research.

claims.claim: Ex can form a complex with Kib in S2 cells.
claims.source: Although Ex can form a complex with Kib in S2 cells (Genevet et al., 2010; Yu et al., 2010) and Kib junctional localization is dependent on Crb (Su et al., 2017), our results show that depletion of Crb, Ex, Ft, or Tao-1 does not affect Kib-GFP levels.
claims.evidence: This is supported by citations to prior research.

claims.claim: Kib junctional localization is dependent on Crb.
claims.source: Although Ex can form a complex with Kib in S2 cells (Genevet et al., 2010; Yu et al., 2010) and Kib junctional localization is dependent on Crb (Su et al., 2017), our results show that depletion of Crb, Ex, Ft, or Tao-1 does not affect Kib-GFP levels.
claims.evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior research.

claims.claim: Depletion of Crb, Ex, Ft, or Tao-1 does not affect Kib-GFP levels.
claims.source: Although Ex can form a complex with Kib in S2 cells (Genevet et al., 2010; Yu et al., 2010) and Kib junctional localization is dependent on Crb (Su et al., 2017), our results show that depletion of Crb, Ex, Ft, or Tao-1 does not affect Kib-GFP levels.
claims.evidence: This is a summary of experimental findings from the study.

claims.claim: Kib degradation is triggered by Kib-mediated complex formation.
claims.source: Together with our results that Hpo and Wts promote Kib ubiquitination independently of their kinase activity (Figure 2I), these data strongly suggest that Kib degradation is triggered by Kib-mediated complex formation.
claims.evidence: This is an inference drawn from multiple experimental findings.

claims.claim: Kib is phosphorylated at S677 upon formation of the signaling complex by an as yet unidentified kinase.
claims.source: Given the importance of the putative phospho-degron in Kib turnover, we propose that Kib is phosphorylated at S677 upon formation of the signaling complex by an as yet unidentified kinase, leading to the recruitment of SCFSlimb and Kib ubiquitination.
claims.evidence: This is a proposed model based on the experimental findings.

claims.claim: Loss of Ex or Crb has no effect on Kib abundance because they do not participate in Kib-mediated signaling complexes.
claims.source: This model potentially explains the striking compartmentalization of Kib degradation that we observe—loss of Ex or Crb has no effect on Kib abundance because they do not participate in Kib-mediated signaling complexes.
claims.evidence: This is an inference drawn from the experimental observations.

claims.claim: Junctional tension is greater at the periphery of the wing pouch.
claims.source: Previous studies have shown that junctional tension also is greater at the periphery of the wing pouch (Legoff et al., 2013; Mao et al., 2013).
claims.evidence: This is supported by citations to prior research.

claims.claim: Higher tension at the wing pouch periphery has been proposed to drive tissue growth as a compensatory mechanism for low levels of diffusible morphogens.
claims.source: Higher tension at the wing pouch periphery has been proposed to drive tissue growth, possibly by promoting Yki function, as a compensatory mechanism for low levels of diffusible morphogens that are expressed in narrow bands of cells at the center of the pouch (Shraiman, 2005; Aegerter-Wilmsen et al., 2007; Hariharan, 2015; Pan et al., 2018).
claims.evidence: This is supported by citations to prior research.

claims.claim: Junctional tension represses Hpo pathway activity via inhibition of Wts.
claims.source: Interestingly, junctional tension is known to repress Hpo pathway activity via inhibition of Wts (Lats1/2 in mammals; Rauskolb et al., 2014; Ibar et al., 2018), though it remains unknown whether junctional tension also affects upstream Hpo pathway regulators such as Kib.
claims.evidence: This is supported by citations to prior research.

claims.claim: Tension promotes Kib degradation and thereby reduces Kib-mediated upstream pathway activation.
claims.source: Given our results, we propose that tension also promotes Kib degradation and thereby reduces Kib-mediated upstream pathway activation.
claims.evidence: This is a proposed model based on the experimental findings.

claims.claim: Kib ubiquitination and degradation can be uncoupled from activation of pathway kinases.
claims.source: However, our results using kinase-dead forms of Hpo and Wts clearly suggest that Kib ubiquitination and degradation can be uncoupled from activation of pathway kinases.
claims.evidence: This is an inference drawn from the experimental findings with kinase-dead mutants.

claims.claim: Tension might regulate access of the degradation components to Kib-organized signaling complexes.
claims.source: We imagine that tension might regulate access of the degradation components (e.g. the putative kinase or SCFSlimb) to Kib-organized signaling complexes and thereby regulate Kib-mediated pathway activation.
claims.evidence: This is a speculative model proposed by the authors.

claims.claim: Transcriptional negative feedback can serve to limit the output of a signaling pathway over time.
claims.source: Feedback regulation is a common feature in cell signaling, and transcriptional negative feedback can serve to limit the output of a signaling pathway over time (Perrimon and McMahon, 1999).
claims.evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior research.

claims.claim: Transcriptional feedback mediated by Yki is not specific to Kib.
claims.source: In the case of the Hpo pathway, transcriptional feedback mediated by Yki is not specific to Kib, as Ex and Mer expression is also promoted by Yki activity.
claims.evidence: This is based on established knowledge about Yki-mediated transcriptional feedback.

claims.claim: Loss of any upstream Hpo pathway regulator would presumably affect Kib levels via the transcriptional feedback.
claims.source: Moreover, loss of any upstream Hpo pathway regulator, including Ex, Crb, Ft, or Tao-1 would presumably affect Kib levels via the transcriptional feedback.
claims.evidence: This is an inference based on the understanding of transcriptional feedback mechanisms.

claims.claim: The post-translational feedback silences Kib function in a more rapid and specific manner than transcriptional feedback.
claims.source: In contrast, the post-translational feedback identified in this study would silence Kib function in a more rapid and specific manner.
claims.evidence: This is an inference drawn from the properties of post-translational versus transcriptional regulation.

claims.claim: The role of the post-translational feedback could be to enhance the robustness of Kib-mediated signaling.
claims.source: The role of the post-translational feedback could be to enhance the robustness of Kib-mediated signaling (Stelling et al., 2004), possibly by preventing drastic fluctuations in Kib levels, to ensure optimally scaled and patterned tissue growth.
claims.evidence: This is a speculative interpretation supported by a citation to prior research on feedback robustness.

results.result: Loss of Mer leads to higher Kib levels than loss of Ex, despite Ex loss causing greater Yki nuclear accumulation and transcriptional activity. This suggests Kib is regulated by a non-transcriptional mechanism in addition to Yki-mediated feedback.
results.evaluation: Claims C35-C43 provide converging evidence from multiple reporters (endogenous Kib::GFP, Yki-YFP localization, ban3>GFP) showing differential effects of Mer vs Ex loss. The data clearly demonstrate that Kib upregulation in Mer clones cannot be explained solely by transcriptional feedback (C44-C45), supported by Figure 1A-H.

results.result: The Hpo pathway regulates Kib levels independently of Yki/Sd-mediated transcription, as demonstrated by Kib upregulation in sd;Mer and sd;hpo double mutants where Yki transcriptional activity is blocked.
results.evaluation: Claims C46-C47 and C59-C63 provide strong genetic evidence using sd mutants to block Yki transcriptional output. The observation that Kib levels remain elevated in sd;Mer and sd;hpo clones (Figure 1I-J', Figure 2F-G''') definitively demonstrates Yki-independent regulation.

results.result: Kib expressed from a Yki-insensitive ubiquitin promoter (Ubi>Kib-GFP) is upregulated upon depletion of Hpo pathway components (Mer, Sav, Hpo, Wts), confirming non-transcriptional regulation.
results.evaluation: Claims C52-C56 demonstrate that Kib regulation occurs independently of transcription using the ubiquitin promoter system. The control experiment with Ubi>RFP (C55-C56) validates that the promoter is not Yki-responsive, making this a clean test of post-translational regulation (Figure 2B-E).

results.result: Kib is phosphorylated and ubiquitinated in a Hpo pathway-dependent manner, with depletion of Hpo or Wts reducing both modifications.
results.evaluation: Claims C64-C70 provide biochemical evidence from gel shift assays (C64-C66) and ubiquitination assays (C67-C68) showing pathway-dependent post-translational modifications. The data in Figure 2H-I directly demonstrate these modifications, though the specific kinase responsible for phosphorylation remains unidentified.

results.result: Slimb directly regulates Kib stability through a conserved degron motif (676DSGVFE681), with Slimb depletion increasing Kib levels and reducing Kib ubiquitination.
results.evaluation: Claims C71-C81 establish Slimb as the E3 ligase for Kib through multiple lines of evidence: RNAi screen (C71), sequence analysis (C74), co-IP (C76), and ubiquitination assays (C75). The Ex co-depletion control (C72) rules out indirect effects, supporting direct regulation (Figure 3A-D).

results.result: Mutation of the degron serine (KibS677A) stabilizes Kib protein, increases its abundance in vivo, enhances growth suppression, and renders Kib ubiquitination insensitive to Hpo pathway inactivation.
results.evaluation: Claims C77-C83 demonstrate the functional importance of the degron through multiple assays: reduced Slimb binding (C77), reduced ubiquitination (C78, C82), increased protein levels (C79), enhanced phenotype (C80), and pathway insensitivity (C82-C83). The data in Figure 3D-J provide strong support for degron-mediated regulation.

results.result: Wild-type Kib is upregulated both apically and basally in Mer and hpo clones, while KibS677A shows only mild apical stabilization in Mer clones and differential localization in hpo clones (apical increase, basal decrease).
results.evaluation: Claims C84-C90 demonstrate in vivo validation of the degron mechanism using mutant clones. The differential behavior of wild-type vs KibS677A (Figure 4A-P) supports both degron-mediated degradation and cortical recruitment as mechanisms affecting Kib levels. The interpretation of apical recruitment (C90) is reasonable given the data.

results.result: Kib degradation is highly compartmentalized within the Hpo pathway: depletion of Ex, Crb, Ft, Ds, or Tao-1 does not affect Kib levels, while depletion of Mats or Pez increases Kib levels.
results.evaluation: Claims C91-C95 demonstrate pathway compartmentalization through systematic testing of different upstream components (Figure 5A-C', Figure 5—supplement 1A-G). The selective effects support the conclusion that Kib degradation is specific to the pathway components with which it directly interacts.

results.result: Ubi>Kib-GFP can rescue ex null lethality, producing viable fertile flies with larger wings than heterozygotes, demonstrating that Kib and Ex function in parallel.
results.evaluation: Claims C96-C98 provide genetic evidence for parallel function through rescue experiments. The complete rescue of lethality with expected frequencies (Figure 5—supplement 1I-K') and the wing size phenotype (Figure 5D-E) support the conclusion, though the mechanism of rescue is not fully elucidated.

results.result: Kinase-dead versions of Hpo (HpoK71R) and Wts (WtsK743R) can restore Kib ubiquitination when endogenous kinases are depleted, indicating that these kinases promote Kib ubiquitination via complex formation rather than direct phosphorylation.
results.evaluation: Claims C99-C100 provide strong evidence using kinase-dead mutants that Hpo and Wts function structurally rather than enzymatically in Kib ubiquitination (Figure 2I). This is a key mechanistic insight, though it raises questions about which kinase phosphorylates the degron.

results.result: Structure-function analysis reveals that the C-terminal region (aa 858-1288) is dispensable for degradation, while the N-terminal 483 amino acids are essential for both pathway-mediated degradation and pathway activation.
results.evaluation: Claims C102-C107 map functional domains through systematic truncation analysis (Figure 6—supplement 1A-K). The data clearly show that the degron alone is insufficient (C104-C105) and that the N-terminus is required for both degradation and function (C106), though the specific molecular mechanisms remain unclear.

results.result: The WW domains of Kib are necessary for its degradation via the Hpo pathway, as deletion of WW domains stabilizes Kib and renders it insensitive to Hpo depletion, despite maintaining Slimb interaction.
results.evaluation: Claims C108-C113 identify the WW domains as critical for degradation through deletion analysis (Figure 6B-D''). The observation that WW domain deletions prevent degradation despite maintaining Slimb binding (C111-C113) strongly supports the requirement for complex formation beyond simple degron recognition.

results.result: Slimb co-immunoprecipitates with Mer, Hpo, and Wts, and WW domain deletion affects Kib interactions with pathway components (enhanced Mer binding, weakened Wts binding).
results.evaluation: Claims C114-C117 provide biochemical evidence for complex formation between Slimb and pathway components (Figure 6—supplement 2B-F). The differential effects of WW domain deletion on different interactions (C115-C116) suggest complex regulation, though the functional significance requires further investigation.

results.result: Kib degradation occurs in a patterned manner across the wing pouch, with wild-type Kib showing higher abundance centrally and lower peripherally, while KibS677A is distributed uniformly. KibS677A expression causes disproportionate growth inhibition in proximal regions.
results.evaluation: Claims C118-C122 demonstrate spatial patterning of Kib degradation using identical transgenes at the same genomic location (Figure 7A-D). The differential distribution (C118-C119) and the proximal growth defect with KibS677A (C121) support patterned degradation, though the inference about protein turnover (C120) is reasonable but not directly demonstrated.

results.result: Kib degradation is patterned by mechanical tension, as evidenced by increased Kib levels in bantam-expressing clones (which have reduced tension) and the similarity to known tension patterns. KibΔWW1 is insensitive to this regulation.
results.evaluation: Claims C123-C127 link Kib degradation to mechanical tension through bantam clone experiments (Figure 7E-I'). The increased Kib in bantam clones (C124) and insensitivity of WW domain mutants (C126) support tension-dependent regulation. However, the mechanism is indirect and the comparison to prior tension studies (C123) is correlative rather than causative.

results.result: Ubi>Kib-GFP localizes correctly to junctional and medial cortex, causes mild wing undergrowth consistent with pathway activation, but only partially rescues kibra null lethality.
results.evaluation: Claims C48-C51 validate the Ubi>Kib-GFP transgene as a functional tool (Figure 2—supplement 1A-B). The localization and phenotypic data support functionality, though the partial rescue (C51) suggests expression levels may be suboptimal in some tissues.

results.result: Ex is more potent than Mer at inhibiting Yki nuclear translocation, consistent with Ex's ability to directly sequester Yki at the junctional cortex.
results.evaluation: Claim C36 is an inference that contradicts the observed data - if Mer loss caused greater Yki activity, Kib levels should be higher in Mer clones due to transcriptional feedback, but the opposite is observed. Claims C39-C40 correctly interpret the Yki localization data, but C36 appears to be an error in the manuscript's logic.

results.result: The authors propose a model where Kib is phosphorylated at S677 by an unidentified kinase upon signaling complex formation, leading to SCFSlimb recruitment and ubiquitination. This explains why Ex/Crb loss doesn't affect Kib levels.
results.evaluation: Claims C140-C142 present a mechanistic model that is consistent with the data but remains speculative. The identity of the kinase that phosphorylates S677 is unknown (C141), and while the model explains compartmentalization (C142), it requires validation through identification of the kinase and direct demonstration of phosphorylation at S677.

results.result: The authors propose that mechanical tension promotes Kib degradation and that tension might regulate access of degradation machinery to Kib-organized complexes, with degradation uncoupled from kinase activation.
results.evaluation: Claims C146-C148 present speculative models about tension-mediated regulation. While C147 is supported by the kinase-dead experiments, the specific mechanism by which tension regulates degradation (C148) is entirely speculative and requires experimental validation.

results.result: Background information on the Hippo pathway structure, function, and regulation, including its role in tissue growth, the core kinase cassette, upstream regulators, and known feedback mechanisms.
results.evaluation: Claims C1-C34 provide established background knowledge about the Hippo pathway, supported by appropriate citations to prior literature. These claims establish the context for the current study and are well-supported by the cited references.

results.result: Ex upregulation upon Hpo pathway inactivation is Yki-dependent, and the increase in Kib levels is not mediated via Ex, as demonstrated by differential behavior in sd;hpo double mutants.
results.evaluation: Claims C57-C61 distinguish between Ex and Kib regulation mechanisms using sd;hpo double mutants (Figure 2F-G'''). The differential Yki-dependence of Ex vs Kib upregulation provides strong evidence that Kib regulation is not mediated through Ex.

results.result: Kib contains multiple functional domains including two WW domains, a C2-like domain, an aPKC-binding domain, and three coiled-coil regions.
results.evaluation: Claim C101 describes the known domain structure of Kibra based on established knowledge and sequence analysis (Figure 6A). This is well-established background information.

results.result: Summary of the main findings: the Hpo pathway negatively regulates Kib levels via post-translational feedback independent of Yki transcription, involving pathway-dependent phosphorylation and SCFSlimb-mediated ubiquitination.
results.evaluation: Claims C128-C133 summarize the major findings of the study. These summary claims are well-supported by the collective experimental evidence presented throughout the manuscript.

results.result: Discussion of prior work showing relationships between pathway components (Crb-Ex, Ft-Ex, Tao-1-Ex, Ex-Kib, Crb-Kib) and the current finding that depletion of these components doesn't affect Kib levels.
results.evaluation: Claims C134-C139 integrate prior knowledge with current findings to highlight the compartmentalization of Kib regulation. The citations support the prior work, and C139 summarizes the key experimental finding from this study.

results.result: Prior studies have shown that junctional tension is greater at the wing pouch periphery, has been proposed to drive growth as compensation for low morphogen levels, and represses Hpo pathway activity via Wts inhibition.
results.evaluation: Claims C143-C145 cite prior research on mechanical tension in the wing disc. These are well-established findings from the cited literature that provide context for interpreting the current results.

results.result: Discussion of feedback regulation in signaling: transcriptional feedback is common and non-specific in the Hpo pathway, while the post-translational feedback identified here is more rapid and specific, potentially enhancing robustness.
results.evaluation: Claims C149-C153 discuss the functional significance of having dual feedback mechanisms. C149 and C150 are supported by prior knowledge, C151-C152 are reasonable inferences, and C153 is speculative but supported by citation to feedback robustness literature.
